This is a library aggregation of standard hereditary separation properties; May Proposition 6.6 supplies the Hausdorff/regular/completely-regular core, with convention and aggregation changes.

Direct verification: if every subspace of X is normal, then every subspace of a fixed S subset X is normal; hereditary T1 gives the T5 clause.
Perfect normality is standardly hereditary; this version exposes countable choice and uses the library convention separating T6 from perfect normality.

The university topology text proves that every regular Lindelof space is normal, but its definitions build T1 into both regular and normal; the library uses the separation-only convention, so the sourced theorem is semantically supporting rather than exact.
The source defines the topology on R by the basis of half-open intervals [a,b), exactly the construction here.
The Encyclopedia states the Sorgenfrey line is perfectly normal and hereditarily Lindelof; the library isolates clopenness/regularity and makes its countable-choice use explicit.
The Encyclopedia states the stronger perfect normality of the Sorgenfrey line; this corollary records normality with the library choice hypothesis.

The peer-reviewed source states the relative Jones lemma as the same power-set inequality for a dense set and a closed discrete relatively normal subspace; normality supplies relative normality, and the library writes the AC use explicitly.
The sources identify the separable Sorgenfrey plane and its uncountable closed-discrete antidiagonal; the library names Q squared and records the cardinal equivalence.
The sources state that the Sorgenfrey line is normal/perfectly normal while its square is not normal; the library exposes the cardinal proof and AC hypothesis.
The source gives the deleted Tychonoff plank as a nonnormal subspace of the compact Hausdorff plank; the library adds the regular/open profile and explicit countable-choice accounting.
The deleted plank is the standard counterexample; this item repackages it as a general nonheredity conclusion with explicit choice.
The nonimplication is established by standard counterexamples; the library states the tempting false universal under its bare-regular convention and refutes it locally.

Compact Hausdorff spaces are standardly Tychonoff and normal; the library adds explicit DC and the Urysohn-separation conclusion.

Direct verification: 1/x is continuous on (0,1] and unbounded near zero, whereas any continuous extension would be bounded on compact [0,1].
